This is a WIP PR to migrate PyFR to a task graph interface for scheduling kernels.  Using a task graph opens up opportunities for reducing Python overhead (CUDA, HIP, OpenMP) and enabling parallel execution of kernels (CUDA, HIP, OpenCL).  All of this improves strong scaling.

Most of the code is in place, with the PR itself being blocked on ROCm 5 which has the required graph embedding API (until then only GiMMiK is functional on HIP).

author: nateweller
body: #### Changes proposed in this Pull Request The objective of this PR is to remove the use of a fixed constant for calculating introductory pricing discounts on the [Jetpack pricing page](https://cloud.jetpack.com/pricing/), and replace it with data from the new `/introductory-offers` endpoint ( D72857-code ). Task: 1201295898168937-as-1201654603947464 * Ensures the data is loaded by triggering a query for intro offers in `` * Retrieves intro offer price and loading state in `useItemPrice()`. * Removes consideration of introductory offers from `useCouponDiscount()`, as the `discountedPrice` parameter already has the intro discount applied to it. * Passes intro offer loading state from initial call of `useItemPrice()` all the way down into `` to ensure the price placeholder remains active until the intro offer data has been fetched. * Updates `getCurrencyObject()` to add support for formatting numbers that round up. Currently, values such as `4.999...` would be displayed as `4.00` instead of `5.00`. #### Notes * Prices from the `/introductory-offers` endpoint are yearly, while the pricing page displays them as monthly. This PR divides the provided values by 12, and then rounds up the cents (i.e. `9.991` will still round up to `10.00` as not to advertise a lower than actual monthly cost). * After adjusting `getCurrencyObject()` to support rounding numbers, I then made that fix irrelevant for this PR via 59d80f91ce42bf985957ff2e35412461aacd7707. I've kept the change though, as I think it makes `getCurrencyObject()` more robust. I noticed as well that even still, due to floating point numbers there will still be certain number values that will not be rounded correctly by `getCurrencyObject()` or the deeper `numberFormat()` function. I've drafted a new PR (#60411) to detail and discuss if these package functions should be able to handle any valid number thrown at them, and some paths forward in tackling that. * This PR **does not address** the copy on the page i.e. "Get 50% off your first year". #### Testing instructions * Check out this PR * Run `yarn start-jetpack-cloud` and visit http://jetpack.cloud.localhost:3000/pricing * Open the Network tab * Validate the `introductory-offers` XHR request is successful. * Compare the data from the `introductory-offers` endpoint with the discounted prices displayed on the screen. Each price should be divided into 12 months and accurately rounded to the nearest cents value. * Compare the original and discounted price for each product, and validate that the discount badge (i.e. 50% off) is accurate. * Using redux dev tools, validate that the prices are not displayed until the `SITE_INTRO_OFFER_REQUEST_SUCCESS` action has fired. * Visit http://jetpack.cloud.localhost:3000/pricing/monthly and ensure that the introductory offer pricing is **not** applied.

author: tnorling
body:
`handleRedirectPromise` clears the current hash before processing the redirect response. Today this logic doesn't care if the hash came from the current url or from the cache. This causes problems for hash routing scenarios where a custom (non-msal) hash may be removed, causing a route change before the hash can be processed.

This PR fixes this behavior by only clearing the current hash if it contains known response properties 

Fixes #4400

author: evalir
body:
Makes the Portal UI compatible with Gigastakes. Namely:
- From now on, users won't select a chain anymore when creating an app. They'll have a dropdown available on the UI to just get the endpoint for the chain they wanna use once they create it.
- Users won't see how much POKT is staked or whatnot with gigastake-based apps. They'll just get their max relays.
- Every time a new endpoint is made, a dummy Pocket account is made as well. This lets us attach metrics properly.

body:
## Description
- Implementing the API that both shuffles & assigns roles, depending on user's preferences. 

- Built next to & independent from `maakep happen` so that the maakep happen experience remains authentic. It can easily be built into that one too though, if this PoC turns out to be appreciated.

- I did some reorganizing of the audio clips & formatting of code (but kept the laggan copy-righted comments & swenglish of course). If there are undesired, I will simply omit the commits - no problem.

## How to test

1. Update `config.json` by adding this line:

```
{
       "token": "blablasomething",
--->   "dotaPrefsBaseUrl": "GET ADDRESS FROM ME"    <---
}
```

2. In discord, where bot lives, write & verify that you get expected output:

- `!dota set maakep 4 5 fill 1 2 3`
- `!dota roll maakep mbar jorel `
- `!dota delete maakep`
- `!dota link`

3. You can visit the site to verify the data.

4. ???

5. Profit


## Known issues
- Not in this implementation but the root implementation doesn't fully respect the rules of fill, it will add people last in the queue. So if you're rolled for last and fill, you will still get the last pick, but should actually be first.

author: brittanyirl
body: ## Context Video posters aren't getting rendered on canvas (have to hit play in order for it to render). | Safari | Chrome/Firefox | | --- | --- | | | | ## Summary Now when you load a story with video in safari you get to see their poster images. ## Relevant Technical Choices The `video` element that's in charge of canvas videos needed to get its `preload` tag updated from `metadata`. Even though specs say Safari can use the preload tag, that browser treats 'metadata' differently from others? We're using `all` as the preload value in the gif `video` implementation so I opted to use that for the video tag here. It's the same as putting down `auto` or `true` or `akldfjlafdjlakdfjlaksf` because it's just the default value. ## To-do I remember seeing a ticket for this, I will track it down again, but sometimes the images rendered in the footer on safari will still have the pesky gray rectangle for video. It's a separate issue from this but I wanted to mention it. ## User-facing changes Videos will load poster now on canvas in safari. ## Testing Instructions Open the editor and add video (local, 3p), see that you don't get a gray rectangle. Now save and refresh and note that the video posters still load (no gray rectangle in canvas). - [ ] This is a non-user-facing change and requires no QA This PR can be tested by following these steps: 1. ## Reviews ### Does this PR have a security-related impact? ### Does this PR change what data or activity we track or use? ### Does this PR have a legal-related impact? ## Checklist - [x] This PR addresses an existing issue and I have linked this PR to it in ZenHub - [x] I have tested this code to the best of my abilities - [x] I have verified accessibility to the best of my abilities ([docs](https://github.com/google/web-stories-wp/blob/main/docs/accessibility-testing.md)) - [x] I have verified i18n and l10n (translation, right-to-left layout) to the best of my abilities - [ ] This code is covered by automated tests (unit, integration, and/or e2e) to verify it works as intended ([docs](https://github.com/google/web-stories-wp/tree/main/docs#testing)) - [x] I have added documentation where necessary - [x] I have added a matching `Type: XYZ` label to the PR --- Fixes #10167

author: wagoodman
body:
This PR does primarily enhances up support for OS-related packages to include distro version information in any pURL generated:
```diff
- pkg:alpine/name@1.0.1?arch=amd64
+ pkg:alpine/name@1.0.1?arch=amd64&distro=alpine-3.4.6
```
The `ID` and `VersionID` are encoded into the pURL as a `distro` get-param; see [the pURL spec](https://github.com/package-url/purl-spec/blob/master/PURL-TYPES.rst#deb) for more info. 

Additionally this PR:
- migrates the existing package URL functionality to the `pkg` package (since this semantically represents packages)
- beefs up testing around pURL generation to ensure that we are exercising all package types
- during this work it was found that the NPM metadata filename within `pkg` was inconsistent --the filename was updated

Related to https://github.com/anchore/grype/issues/395

Note: this PR cannot be merged until https://github.com/anchore/syft/pull/753 is merged and this PR is rebased.

author: steers
body:
`(*Enumeration).filterTaskFunc` creates a new `stringset.Set` for use in the anonymous function it returns, but since `Close()` is never called on this set, the goroutine spawned by `stringset.New` will never return.

Any users leveraging Amass as a library would be subject to one leaked goroutine (and associated memory) after each enumeration run.

Scoping this `stringset.Set` to the lifetime of an Enumeration would allow it to be closed properly, with no impact to functionality, by passing it as an argument to `filterTaskFunc`.

author: kartg
body:
### Description
This change consists of two commits:

1. __Prevent Lucene indexing operations on replica__
  This change prevents Lucene indexing operations from occurring on replicas, while still writing to the replica translog. Note that the change only affects indexing operations. The logic in IndexShard has been changed to only write to the translog when applying the indexing operation to a replica shard. To allow this, a new addIndexOperationToTranslog API is exposed on the Engine class, which InternalEngine implements using existing translog logic. This code change also refactors the existing indexing logic in InternalEngine into separate internal methods - one that parses the document and prepares the Index object, and another for error handling.
2. __Added index setting for segment replication__
  For now, this is a boolean final value that simply turns segment replication on/off. The logic in IndexShard has been updated to branch based on this value.

author: jsteemann
body:
### Scope & Purpose

This PR refactors a few components:
* remove unused `_keyOptions` member in LogicalCollection
* clean up ExpressionContext a bit
* remove basics::StringBuffer from several places and use std::string instead, e.g.
  * transaction::Context::leaseStringBuffer()
  * transaction::Context::returnStringBuffer()
  * several RestHandlers
  * Aql/Functions.cpp
* adding operator* to transaction::BuilderLeaser and transaction::StringLeaser
* remove `isDataFromCollection()` function from ExpressionContext. the previous `isDataFromCollection` flag in Aql/Variable.cpp is now renamed to `isFullDocumentFromCollection` and set for a few more ExecutionNode types than before
* rename a few constructors for AqlValue to use more appropriate names
* add Function::canUseInAnalyzer enum value, so that functions can be marked as usable/unusable inside arangosearch analyzers. this allows removal an extra list of forbidden AQL functions from the analyzer code
* make methods in Expression static so that they only rely on their input values and cannot modify the Expression object. this is a refactoring for making Expression more thread-safe to use in later use cases
* move standalone Expression execution from analyzer code (arangod/IResearch/IResearchAqlAnalyzer.cpp) to arangod/Aql/StandaloneCalculation.cpp. the moved code will likely be called from other components too and will not be iresearch-specific anymore.

This will not be backported.

author: teunbrand
body:
Hi Alan,

This PR attempts to fix the problem described in #60. It does so by rescaling `hjust` such that it can be interpreted as the justification along the direction of the text in the visible part of the line. Example below:

``` r
library(geomtextpath)
#> Loading required package: ggplot2
library(patchwork)

df <- data.frame(slope = c(0.25, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, -1),
                 intercept = c(0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0.5))

plot_hjust <- function(hjust = 0.5) {
  force(hjust)
  ggplot(df) +
    geom_textabline(aes(slope = slope, label = slope, intercept = intercept),
                    hjust = hjust) +
    lims(x = c(0, 1), y = c(0, 1)) +
    labs(subtitle = paste0("hjust = ", hjust))
}

plot_hjust(0.25) + plot_hjust(0.5) + plot_hjust(0.75)
```
